issues.title: A container built by a command with no value route (`lrange`, `lreverse`, `lrepeat`, `concat`, `join`) is never a proven value for diagnostics: W230 is silent after `set l [lrange …]` where the optimiser folds it
A `::name` write in the top-level body does not alias the plain `name`, so O102, O109 and O100 fold the stale value
A `proc` whose namespace does not exist is taken as defined, where every tclsh raises `unknown namespace`
A `proc` replacing an ensemble implementation (`::tcl::dict::size`) does not stop the O129 fold of `dict size` or its qualified spelling (miscompile)
W220 false positive: a caller's local is reported never read when a callee writes a same-named namespace variable through `variable`
A callee's write through a `::`-qualified `upvar` name argument, or a caller's `upvar #0` alias passed as one, is not a global write: the top level forwards and deletes the stale store (miscompile)
A procedure's global-write summary misses a plain write inside its `namespace eval ::` body, so a caller's read of that global is folded
Writes inside a `catch` body nested in a command substitution are invisible to the value lattice: wrong I230 and false W210
An iRules `when` handler's binding walk runs in `::when` while its binding sites are recorded in `::`, so every command in the handler looks unbound
Subcommand availability gates in both runtimes answer one question three ways (release name, surface profile name, gate profile)
runtime/rust: `upvar 1` from a procedure called inside `namespace eval` cannot read the namespace-eval frame's variable
SSA treats `::name` and `name` as different places at the top level: wrong I230/O112 fold, false W210 and W211
tcl-vm: the `Namespace` and `UnknownHandling` guard domains move on fewer events than the runtime's, and `namespace unknown` never invalidates
tclvm: `interp alias` with a qualified alias name does not create the namespace, and the two-argument describe form is missing
tclvm: a qualified interp alias under a new parent namespace is not dispatchable
`namespace upvar`'s `otherVar` word carries no `ArgRole`, so every role-driven consumer is blind to the word that names the aliased cell
hover.rs keeps a dead, test-only hover path that recognises `format`/`scan`/`regexp`/`regsub`/`clock` by whitespace-token spelling under a standing `#[allow(dead_code)]`
O103 folds a pure-proc call without the `expr`-trust gate O110 consults: a shadowed `expr` is evaluated as the builtin
Replace non-injective flat command/namespace keys for colon-edge Tcl names
O129 never folds `[self class]` in the spelling anyone actually writes
clay::define declares no class to the analyser, so nothing in a clay-based file navigates
Key compiler effect summaries by stable procedure generation
Retain compiled descendant command tokens across activation-delayed parent namespace deletion
Use structured payloads for all diagnostics and eliminate message parsing in consumers
runtime/rust: "invalid command name" carries `-errorcode NONE` where C Tcl gives `TCL LOOKUP COMMAND name`
An unscoped pack `-override` loses to a scoped shipped spec in every profile-aware lookup (`best_visible` prefers scoped specs)
A relative builtin spelling (`tcl::dict::set d k v`) is unknown to the registry, so its store is deleted as unread
tclvm: missing tcl::unsupported::representation blocks real format-20.1
`::tcl::dict::with` draws W002 and W211 under `tcl8.6` where `dict with` draws neither
`existStk` re-resolves an already-resolved braced variable name, so `info exists {{zz}}` answers 0
W210 false triggering
O125 code sinking moves a store past an intervening write or an unseen call in the target body (miscompile)
iRules: a `sharedvar` variable's writes are deleted as unused or dead stores, with false W211 and W220 (miscompile)
O126 removes a bare write to a `::`-qualified `variable`'s tail as an unused assignment, and W211 reports it (miscompile)
A module that rebinds any builtin has no transfer summaries for any of its procedures
O103 folds a builtin's call through a same-named `proc` defined later in the file, where the earlier call ran the builtin (miscompile)
A same-frame `upvar 0` alias write is not a write of its target: false I230 and W241
W220 false positive: a global assignment read by a procedure through `upvar` is reported as never read
tclvm: portable package command validation and discovery differ from Tcl 9
tclvm: interp create treats a multi-component interpreter path as a literal child name
tclvm: child interpreter commands lack alias and aliases subcommands
tclvm test runner: forward focused test arguments to child interpreters through argv
tclvm: interp exists and issafe ignore nested interpreter paths
tclvm: real Tcl 9 package.test cannot autoload ::pkg::create
tclvm: children of a safe interpreter are created unsafe by default
`make rust-check` never runs the dialect-drift gate: `xtask-dialect-drift` sits after the `##` help comment on the `xtask-check` line, and 8 sites on `rust` fail it
Stub sidecar flags are parsed and dropped: `StubFlags` has no consumer
Centralize compiler frame reach and preserve exact composed eval, uplevel, and upvar distance
Post-release: adversarial audit and normalization of command semantics
Flaky e2e test under load: `workspace_symbol_waits_out_the_startup_scan` (tcl-lsp-server document_symbols)
`! $x contains "y"`: the compiler and the iRule harness group a prefix operator before a custom comparison differently, and neither grouping is measured
`regsub -all {}` on a supplementary scalar counts positions by scalar, not by the release's character model
server: the LSP server stops answering everything for ~100s under concurrent load, after pack-association churn
O100 reports inlining a proved read inside a quoted word but the rewrite is never applied
An `uplevel 0 {…}` body records no reads or writes, so O126 and O109 delete stores the body reads
